g.text: The backbone compresses video twofold in time
frames sampled at 4 fps (as in evaluation)
vision encoder: every visual patch spans 2 consecutive frames → one set of visual tokens per pair
Why not one candidate per frame?
frame 1 and frame 2 share their visual tokens:
the LLM never sees them apart, so a single-frame
candidate would have nothing of its own to point to
one candidate = 2 / fps seconds: 0.5 s at 4 fps, 1 s at 2 fps
boundaries fall halfway between neighbouring pairs
a 2-minute video at 4 fps → 480 frames → 240 candidates
VideoJev (arXiv:2610.18615), §2.2 and Figure 2 ("The backbone's twofold temporal compression groups frames into pairs."); video of 2.0 s for illustration
